originality.rationale: The main claim is the exact depth-n preimage cardinality E_n for this specified rotating feedback map, not the known no-singleton stable-word criterion. Inspected primary ACRI 2004 work gives stable words and the absence of ordinary sequential cycles, and general counting-complexity sources do not imply this specific preimage formula. Comparisons with indexed and previously published results found similar Lucas stable counts in other models and parity orbit results, not a covering last-clock theorem. Historical-priority uncertainty remains.

value.rationale: The final-clock settling event is a natural dynamic observable for a minimal nonlinear majority-feedback register, and exactly 1/12 of uniformly random inputs asymptotically attain the sharp n-clock settling threshold. This quantitative positive-density long-transient phenomenon is not a textbook restatement of stable-word enumeration. The finite-time census is complete at the sharp endpoint despite unproved earlier-time strata.
